qemu.documentation_basis: QEMU user networking exposes the host at x.x.x.2 and virtual DNS at x.x.x.3 by default; hostfwd redirects incoming host connections to guest endpoints.

reference_cases.operation: pathname AF_UNIX stream server/client exchange with close/reuse negative case
AF_UNIX datagram send/recv for target-required subset
reference_cases.classification: promote to required only if pinned corpus proves mandatory

reference_cases.operation: resolve deterministic fixture name using unchanged glibc resolver; use the QEMU virtual DNS path or an explicitly recorded local DNS fixture, never silently depend on ambient public DNS for acceptance
guest connects to 10.0.2.2:18081; host-local deterministic TCP endpoint replies KERNAL_TCP_OK
guest sends to 10.0.2.2:18082; host-local deterministic UDP endpoint replies with KERNAL_UDP_OK prefix
guest listens on TCP/8080; host reaches 127.0.0.1:18080 through QEMU hostfwd

runtime_owner_rules: one Linux socket semantics owner integrated with kernel/linux-fd
DNS remains ordinary userspace resolver behavior over files + UDP/TCP
NIC transport owns queues, not IP/socket policy
stale socket/device generations cannot redirect old authority to replacement objects
